original_question: Understand how virtual-knot polynomials relate to Vassiliev invariants for virtual knots, and determine whether every finite-type Vassiliev invariant of classical knots extends to a finite-type invariant of long virtual knots in the sense described by the paper, while also clarifying the alternate finite-type notion for virtual knots mentioned there.
target_in_paper: Section 8.5.1, Problem 1, read as the sharpened version of Section 8.1, Problem 19: Problem 19 asks to "understand the connection between virtual knot polynomials and the Vassiliev knot invariants of virtual knots (in Kauffman's sense)," and Section 8.5.1(1) refines the issue to: "Classify all obstructions for a Vassiliev finite-type invariant to be a GPV finite-type invariant."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's finite-type/Vassiliev theme for virtual knots, notices that polynomial invariants are part of the discussion, and recognizes that the paper contrasts Kauffman's Vassiliev notion with an alternate finite-type notion for virtual knots, namely the Goussarov-Polyak-Viro (GPV) notion.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation is not a question about extending every classical-knot finite-type invariant to long virtual knots; in this paper the sharp open problem is Section 8.5.1(1): classify obstructions for a Vassiliev finite-type invariant of virtual knots to be GPV finite-type.

The broader wording actually appearing in the paper is Section 8.1, Problem 19: understand the connection between virtual-knot polynomials and Vassiliev invariants of virtual knots in Kauffman's sense.
The alternate finite-type notion must be named exactly: Goussarov-Polyak-Viro (GPV) finite-type, with the Polyak algebra as the universal invariant on that side.
The relevant objects are oriented virtual knots; your draft introduces long virtual knots, but long virtual knots are not part of the official formulation of Problem 19 or Section 8.5.1(1).

The paper's polynomial evidence is specific: it cites infinitely many different extensions of the Conway polynomial to virtual knots, all satisfying the same skein relation, whose coefficients give an infinite family of Vassiliev finite-type invariants of every order.
A specific known obstruction recorded by the paper is that an integer-valued Vassiliev invariant that is invariant under the virtualization move cannot be GPV finite-type.
No fixed finite order n is part of the official problem; if you want an order-by-order or degree-preserving version, that extra quantifier must be stated explicitly.

If you intended the adjacent lifting problem instead, the paper requires the data Σ compact oriented, G abelian, VK the isotopy classes of oriented virtual knots, K[Σ] the isotopy classes of oriented knots in Σ × I, κ: K[Σ] → VK the projection, and Z[S] the free abelian group on a set S.

The paper's only direct long-knot statement in this vicinity is the natural map from long virtual knots to oriented compact virtual knots, which lets one pull compact invariants back to long ones; that is different from the classical-to-long-virtual extension claim in your draft.
refined_question: For oriented virtual knots, with finite type understood in Kauffman's Vassiliev sense and also in the Goussarov-Polyak-Viro (GPV, Polyak-algebra/arrow-diagram) sense, determine necessary and sufficient obstructions for a Vassiliev finite-type invariant—especially one arising from coefficients of a virtual-knot polynomial extension such as the Conway extensions cited in the paper—to be GPV finite-type; in particular, explain how the polynomial-derived examples fit into Vassiliev theory and account for the known obstruction that any integer-valued Vassiliev invariant invariant under the virtualization move is not GPV finite-type.
justification: The draft is aimed at the right topic but blends together two different levels of formulation in the survey. The exact broad problem matching your opening clause is Section 8.1, Problem 19, which asks for the connection between virtual-knot polynomials and Vassiliev invariants of virtual knots in Kauffman's sense (Section 8.1, Problem 19, P23 / printed 33). The later and sharper paper-faithful formulation is Section 8.5.1(1), where the authors first distinguish GPV finite-type invariants from Vassiliev finite-type invariants, note that GPV invariants are finitely generated at each order while Vassiliev invariants are infinitely generated, cite the infinitely many Conway-polynomial extensions as examples on the Vassiliev side, record virtualization-invariance as an obstruction, and then explicitly ask to classify all obstructions to being GPV finite-type (Section 8.5.1, Problem 1, P41 / printed 51). By contrast, the sentence in your draft about extending every classical finite-type invariant to long virtual knots is not an official problem in this paper. The only nearby long-knot remark is the natural map from long virtual knots to compact virtual knots that allows compact invariants to be viewed as long-knot invariants (Section 2.3, P5 / printed 15), and the only adjacent extension/lifting problem is Section 8.5.1(2), which concerns lifting Vassiliev finite-type invariants of virtual knots to knots in Σ × I via κ, not classical-to-long-virtual extension (Section 8.5.1, Problem 2, P41 / printed 51).
